question: Where is not-all-equal bond distance a metric? Additivity at separating distinctions and the block reduction on random complement-closed bases; rings and cacti; every small pure not-all-equal block; graph-like bases; sparse bases on nine distinctions; tonight's grown bases.

definitions.bond distance: least bond holding both, minus one; infinite when none
definitions.block: biconnected component of the primal graph
definitions.separating distinction: a cut vertex of the primal graph
definitions.graph-like: each distinction in at most two knots, knots meeting at most once

public_inputs.reused: BOND-METRIC's metriclib.py; PICK-TWO's picklib.py and KNOT-SWITCH's knotlib.py for the growth runs, unchanged

forbidden_inputs: Changing cases, readings, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results
primary_observable: P1-P7 (with P1b) of research/NAE-METRIC-20261118-001/preregistration.md, scored by merge.py.
cheapest_meaningful_control: checks.py gates: the split criterion against brute force, the series-parallel test on known graphs, the two-knot exhibit.

predictions.P1b: bond count identity at a separating distinction
predictions.P2: block formula; metric iff every block; no violation spans blocks
predictions.P3: rings 3-9 plain and twisted: b = steps + 1, run counts, largest b
predictions.P5: failing pure NAE blocks (<= 7 distinctions, <= 6 knots) have a double meeting
predictions.P6: graph-like pure NAE bases with a series-parallel knot graph are metric (conjecture)
predictions.P7: grown bases: b <= 2 at every step; the triple criterion agrees with brute force

decision_rules.each prediction: holds or fails as scored by merge.py

stop_rule: One run; read-out; proof; referee hand-off; report.
